newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes drift lower after ANS sold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes drift lower after ANS sold.

text.p: Prices for Alaskan crude on the U.S. West Coast market drifted lower Monday after the sale of a full cargo at a weaker differential, traders said.

A large Northwest refiner bought over 400,000 barrels of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude early Monday at $1.02 under May West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude. The refinery will take delivery sometime in May.

The buyer declined to name the seller on record, but said it was not BP. ANS sold previously at $0.91 cents under WTI, and buyers claimed the differential would weaker as refineries took in high volumes of South American barrels near term.
Over the next two months, Chevron was reportedly buying four cargoes of Ecuadorian crude containing 360,000 barrels each, traders said.

In California markets, producers last week sold spot barrels of California Wilmington crude at 0.85 and 0.79 cents a barrels, traders said, marginally raising the price from a range of $0.70 yo $0.80 cents a gallon.
